text:
Marta: Heads-up — after the 03/10 runtime roll I'm seeing a consistent >99th percentile latency spike on mixed prefill+decode workloads. Prefill appears to be consuming batch tokens and starving decode. attaching quick pprof and logs in thread.

Sam: I noticed the same on canary. Repro on local bench with long prompts (8k prefill); decode tail shoots up. My hunch: kernel selection is favoring a large-batch kernel during handshake, then decode falls back to a slower kernel mid-gen.

Kai: Can you paste the profile snippet?

Marta: sure — ran `pprof --text` on the canary instance, trimmed: 
```
(pprof) top
47.3%  BatchScheduler::form_batch
21.6%  KernelSelector::choose_kernel_for_phase
13.1%  KVCache::restore_entries
7.4%   ContinuousBatcher::token_budget_accounting
4.1%   Decoder::apply_attention_kernels
```
Also saw KV miss spikes during decode steps (miss rate ~0.28, prefill miss ~0.05).

Anya: kv miss that high would explain stalls. Are we draining the KV cache when prefill finishes? Could be aggressive eviction during handshake.

Marta: eviction looks normal, but prefill batches have huge prefix reuse so they warm some shards and then heavy decode bursts read cold shards on different flows.

perf-bot: [alert] 99p latency +18% vs baseline after deploy r2026-03-10T08:14. Canary 10% showing regressed tail.

Sam: proposal: additive heuristic called "token-decay isolation" — maintain a decayed token budget per flow window so recent prefill-heavy flows gradually give up tokens to decode over Y ms. Rough config idea: 
```
# scheduler token-decay config
token_decay_half_life_ms: 1200
min_decode_reserve_tokens: 8
per_flow_max_tokens: 256
phase_weight: { prefill: 0.6, decode: 1.0 }
```
Effect: prevents prefill from immediately monopolizing newly formed batches and gives decode preferential weighting when it has waiting ops.

Kai: +1 on decay; also add a soft isolation window: if decode_wait_ms > 10 then reserve N tokens for decode for the next 50ms. That prevents handshakes from collapsing into one huge prefill batch.

Anya: kernel selector change: factor in `phase_tag` when scoring kernel variants. Right now it scores purely on throughput for large batch sizes; add a penalty when the request is phase==decode and kernel has high init latency. e.g. score *= (1 + phase_penalty) for prefill.

Marta: good call. We should also try routing small decode-only requests to the small-kernel path early (fast-start kernel).

Sam: I'll draft patch to ContinuousBatcher.token_accounting and KernelSelector.score_kernel. Plan: sim with replayed trace, then canary 5% -> 20% if stable.

Marta: add metrics before roll: `tokens_reserved_by_phase`, `tokens_used_by_phase`, `kernel_choice_ratio_by_phase`, `kv_miss_rate_by_shard`. Also add tracing tag `phase_hint` on requests so we can correlate slow traces.

Kai: one more note — in profiling I saw `KVCache::restore_entries` holding a mutex for spikes; consider async restore for decode path if possible.

Anya: for the short term let's limit prefill max_batch_tokens when there are pending decode ops on the queue. That is a simple guard while we iterate on token-decay.

Sam: rolling a sim-run now. If green I'll push a draft PR with tests + bench numbers. Canary planned for end of day.

Marta: thanks — please @me on the PR. Also echoing: if anyone sees this in prod traces, add the trace id here. :thumbsup:
